test_policy.notes: The freshman page labels SAT/ACT optional ('please send official copies'); preferred minimums are SAT EBRW 480 and Math 440, or ACT English or Reading 17 and Math 17. Regular admission uses a Freshman Index of at least 1940 combining high school GPA and test scores; applicants below it can enter through University College (2.0 GPA). The international page lets test scores double as English proof.

requirements.notes: Freshmen apply through the GAfutures portal (the Common App is not mentioned). International applicants also need a NACES or AICE document-by-document evaluation of the high school transcript, the Declaration and Certification of Finances with a bank letter, and a passport copy; allow at least four weeks for processing. The deadline and freshman pages print no application fee (College Navigator lists $25 for 2024-25).

deadlines.label: International student application deadline (fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: Deadlines page: fall July 1, spring November 14, summer April 15 for international students (general undergraduate fall deadline July 21). Dates print without a year; treated as fall 2027. Allow time for the I-20 and visa.

deadlines.label: Freshman scholarship deadline (fall)
deadlines.notes: Also the priority date for the Promise Scholarship and the President Carter Leadership Program. Printed without a year; treated as 2027.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Applicants from or graduating from a school in a non-native English-speaking country may submit TOEFL, IELTS, SAT, ACT, an English Language Institute (ELI) Advanced Completion Certificate, or qualifying Accuplacer scores (Next Gen Reading 237, WritePlacer 4+). Applicants with more than two years of U.S. high school or from a native English-speaking country submit SAT or ACT instead. Duolingo, PTE and Cambridge are not mentioned; the ELI route is a campus English program.

english.notes: Page lists 69 iBT (523 paper, 193 computer). No 1-6 scale value is given. SAT EBRW 480+/Math 440+ or ACT 17/17 also satisfies it.

cost.notes: Non-resident table, 2026-27 header: matriculation $10,200 plus fees = $10,732 per semester (15 credits), so $21,464 per year. Housing and meals use the Oaks double room ($2,608) plus the Unlimited meal plan ($2,230) per semester, doubled; other halls cost more. Health insurance and personal expenses are not included. International students can seek a limited out-of-state tuition waiver worth about $13,000 (see aid).

aid.notes: GSW says it has no scholarships specifically for international students. A limited number of out-of-state tuition waivers (about $13,000 savings) are offered, with priority to students completing the ELI with the Advanced Completion Certificate; the Outstanding Out-of-State Student waiver and Beginning Freshmen Scholarships (Feb. 1) are open to international applicants who send SAT or ACT scores.

toefl.note: No TOEFL institution code is printed on the pages read.
